target_moa.text: Odevixibat is a reversible inhibitor of the ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT), decreasing reabsorption of bile acids (primarily salt forms) from the terminal ileum and thereby reducing the overall bile acid pool

citations.quote: Odevixibat is a reversible inhibitor of the ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT). It decreases the reabsorption of bile acids (primarily the salt forms) from the terminal ileum.
IBATs are intended to reduce the overall bile acid pool (i.e., serum, liver, and intestinal pool).

The molecular formula is C_{37}H_{48}N_4O_8S_2 \times 1.5 H_2O, with a molecular weight of 768.0 g/mol (anhydrous 740.9 g/mol). Odevixibat sesquihydrate is a white to off-white solid. Its solubility in aqueous solutions is pH-dependent and increases with increased pH.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>2%) are liver test abnormalities, diarrhea, abdominal pain, vomiting, and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency. In Trial 1 diarrhea occurred in 10% (placebo), 39.1% (40 mcg/kg) and 21.1% (120 mcg/kg); transaminases increased in 5% (placebo), 13.0% (40 mcg/kg) and 21.1% (120 mcg/kg)

summary.text: BYLVAY was reviewed as a Priority NDA and approved for pruritus in PFIC based on the single phase 3 trial A4250-005. Odevixibat had Orphan Drug Designation (granted 10/31/2012), Fast Track designation (granted July 18, 2018), and Rare Pediatric Disease Designation, and the applicant received a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher. This was a traditional (not accelerated) approval.

citations.quote: Priority or standard	Priority

Odevixibat was granted Rare Pediatric Disease Designation (RPDD) for the treatment of PFIC by the Office of Orphan Products Development on June 04, 2018 (designation RPD-2018-170). Fast Track designation was granted to A4250 (odevixibat) on July 18, 2018 for treatment of pruritus associated with progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis (PFIC).
The Applicant met all criteria for receiving a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher. Notably, labeling will include all patients with PFIC affected by pruritus.
